title: Cortisol
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows your level of cortisol, a hormone made by the adrenal glands.
why: For possible adrenal problems, sudden changes in weight or blood pressure, or strong weakness.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you use steroid hormones: pills, shots, creams, or inhalers
If you take birth control pills
If you work nights or your sleep is irregular

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Cortisol changes during the day. Blood is usually taken in the morning, at the time your doctor sets.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No alcohol, no hard workouts, and no smoking. Try to get a good night's sleep.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

steps: Before the draw, sit quietly for 15 to 30 minutes, if the lab asks you to
You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when
Sometimes the doctor also orders a saliva or urine cortisol test

faq.q: Why does the time of the test matter?
faq.a: Cortisol is higher in the morning and lower in the evening. Your doctor compares your result with the normal range for that time.
Yes, stress raises cortisol. That is why you are asked to rest before the draw.

reminders.text: Cortisol test tomorrow morning. Go to bed early and do not eat after dinner. Come at the time your doctor set.
